inbox_review.scope: Reviewed the complete project inbox and provisional shortlist. Direct primary-source review found Anthropic's October 21 API-version migration stronger and more actionable than the automated winners.

archive_review: Reviewed all 17 episode files and confirmed receipts through October 19. The archive covers Haiku 5.5 model migration but not the new Claude API version 2026-10-21 or its request-level breaking changes.

openai.reason: The October 21 service-tier controls and October 20 twelve-hour prompt cache are timely builder changes, but each needs a separate settings or cost evaluation and neither displaces the breaking Claude migration.

anthropic.reason: Anthropic released API version 2026-10-21 and SDK major versions on October 21. The documented 400-error conditions create an immediate compatibility audit for Messages API builders.

google.reason: The official Gemini API changelog has no newer entry than the October 13 Gemini 4 Argon release, already covered by episode 2026-10-15-gemini-argon-api.

repositories.reason: Recursive Flint is a strong October 21 open-weight coding-agent model and repository lead, but its roughly 80 GB checkpoint and H200/B300 documented serving path require a separate artifact evaluation.

architectures.reason: SPEM is an October 19 research-only procedural-memory architecture with reported benchmark results; the full mechanism and evidence need a dedicated Deep review.

candidates.title: Claude API version 2026-10-21 migration audit
candidates.summary: Anthropic released API version 2026-10-21 and new SDK major versions. Builders must remove sampling parameters, relocate some content blocks and update renamed response fields before switching.
candidates.availability: Available through the Claude API and new SDK major versions. On Amazon Bedrock it is available only for Claude 4.7 and later models.
candidates.practical_use: Audit a Messages API request fixture for sampling parameters, assistant document blocks and user citations, then run it against the new version in staging before deploying.

source_review.excerpt: In 2026-10-21, a request that sends temperature, top_p, or top_k returns a 400 error.
source_review.decision: Release notes and the full migration guide reviewed. This episode will explain the documented compatibility audit without claiming a live API test.
source_review.availability: API version and SDK releases are available now; Bedrock requires Claude 4.7 or later for this version.

candidates.title: OpenAI project service-tier controls and twelve-hour prompt caching
candidates.summary: OpenAI added project and organization service-tier controls on October 21, following twelve-hour prompt caching on October 20.
candidates.availability: Available through OpenAI Platform settings and the Responses API; exact tier eligibility and caching economics vary by project.
candidates.practical_use: Separate latency-sensitive projects from ordinary workloads and evaluate whether long-lived shared prompts justify the cache-write premium.

source_review.excerpt: You can now choose which service tiers projects can use in Platform settings.
source_review.decision: Exact changelog entries reviewed; deferred for a separate configuration and cost decision episode.
source_review.availability: Documented as available in Platform settings and the Responses API.

candidates.title: Recursive Flint open-weight coding-agent model
candidates.summary: Recursive published the Apache-2.0 Flint checkpoint, tokenizer, chat template and SGLang serving kit for coding-agent tasks.
candidates.availability: Public BF16 checkpoint. The documented SGLang path downloads about 80 GB and runs one replica on an H200 or B300 GPU; quantized variants are separate.
candidates.practical_use: Inspect the checkpoint and serving kit, then evaluate repository-level bug fixing in an isolated environment with explicit tool permissions.

source_review.excerpt: This repository contains the BF16 checkpoint, model configuration, tokenizer, chat template, and an SGLang serving kit.
source_review.decision: Model card, setup and limitations reviewed; deferred until the large artifact can receive a dedicated evaluation plan.
source_review.availability: Apache-2.0 checkpoint is public; documented local serving has substantial storage and GPU requirements.

candidates.title: SPEM structure-aware procedural memory for LLM agents
candidates.summary: SPEM proposes atomic skill memory plus reusable skill-DAG memory so agents can select and compose skills with structural context.
candidates.availability: Research paper; no production availability established in this review.
candidates.practical_use: Compare structure-aware skill composition with flat semantic retrieval in a controlled agent benchmark before adopting the memory design.

source_review.excerpt: SPEM maintains Atomic Skill Memory for individual skills and Skill-DAG Memory for reusable compositions
source_review.decision: Abstract, submission date and reported evaluation reviewed; deferred as research-only pending full-paper analysis.

editorial_decisions.reason: Fresh, shipped and immediately actionable for builders, with exact breaking conditions and a safe staging checklist.

editorial_decisions.candidate: OpenAI service tiers and twelve-hour prompt caching
editorial_decisions.reason: Useful but better served by a separate settings and cost evaluation.
Strong artifact lead whose large checkpoint and hardware requirements deserve a dedicated repository/model evaluation.
Research-only mechanism requiring a full-paper Deep review.
